panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: The figure shows a skin biopsy histopathology (10x magnification) demonstrating features compatible with ichthyosiform dermatosis. This pathology is presented in the context of the patient's diagnosis of CHILD syndrome (mentioned in the article title and caption). b: The figure shows a skin biopsy histopathology (40x magnification inset) demonstrating features compatible with ichthyosiform dermatosis. This pathology is presented in the context of the patient's diagnosis of CHILD syndrome (mentioned in the article title and caption).
panels.attribution_text: Estapé et al. Congenital hemidysplasia with ichthyosiform naevus and limb defects (CHILD) syndrome without hemidysplasia.. The British journal of dermatology 2015. doi:10.1111/bjd.13636. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: (a, b) Skin biopsy showing features compatible with ichthyosiform dermatosis: acanthosis and extension of rete pegs of the epidermis, marked parakeratotic scaling with loss of the granular layer, occasional clusters of neutrophils, and perivascular and dermal lymphohistiocytic infiltrates. No verrucous xanthoma was seen. (a) Magnification 10×; (b) magnification 40×.
